title: Spot the AI
about: Tell apps that follow a recipe from AI that learned from examples.

cards.prompt: Your phone learned your face. These two robots sort fruit — how did **Robot B** get good at spotting apples?

image.alt: Two robots sorting a red apple. Robot A holds a recipe card reading red plus round equals apple. Robot B has a stack of apple photos. Both robots say apple.

options.text: By seeing lots of apple photos
A person wrote it a recipe
options.nudge: That's **Robot A** — it holds the recipe card (*red + round = apple*). **Robot B** has a stack of photos it learned from.

cards.hint: Look at what each robot is holding. Robot A has a recipe card. What is Robot B holding?
cards.explanation: **By seeing lots of apple photos.** Robot B was shown example after example until it could spot an apple itself. Robot A instead follows a recipe a person wrote: *red + round = apple*. Both got the red apple — but watch what happens with a trickier one.

cards.prompt: A **green** apple rolls in. Robot A still follows *red + round = apple*. Robot B learned from red **and** green apple photos. Who gets it right?

options.nudge: Robot A's recipe only knows *red*. A green apple isn't red — so what does the recipe decide?
One robot only knows the *red* recipe, and a green apple breaks it.
Robot B saw green apples in its examples, so one of them still gets it right.

cards.hint: Robot A's recipe says *red*. A green apple isn't red — what will the recipe decide?
cards.explanation: **Only Robot B.** Robot A's recipe only knew *red*, so it says *not an apple* — even though it really is one. Robot B saw green apples among its examples, so it still spots this one.

cards.title: Recipe, or learned from examples?
cards.body:
**Robot A follows a recipe** a person wrote: *red + round = apple*. A **calculator** does too. It breaks on anything new.

**Robot B learned from examples** — lots of photos — so it copes with new ones. Your **spam filter** learned the same way. That's **AI**.

cards.prompt: Which of these **follow a recipe**, and which **learned from examples**?
cards.hint: Could a person write down the exact steps? Then it follows a recipe. If it had to learn from lots of cases, it learned from examples.
cards.nudge: A recipe does the same exact steps every time. Learning from examples copes with new cases nobody wrote down.
cards.explanation: A **calculator**, **timed lights** and an **alarm** follow a recipe — exact steps a person set. A **spam filter**, **video recommendations** and **face unlock** learned from examples: there are too many emails, videos and faces to write rules for.

cards.prompt: A new robot must spot **cats** in photos. There are millions of different-looking cats. Which way works?

options.text: Write a recipe for every kind of cat
options.nudge: Could a person write a rule for *every* cat — big, small, fluffy, hairless? There are far too many.

options.text: Show it lots of cat photos until it learns
Let it look each cat up online
options.nudge: It can't look anything up — it has to decide from the photo. How did Robot B get good?

cards.hint: Think of the green apple: a recipe breaks on cases nobody wrote down. What copes with endless variety?
cards.explanation: **Show it lots of cat photos.** Nobody could write a recipe for every cat, just like the recipe missed the green apple. Learning from examples handles endless variety — that's why AI is used for jobs like this.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **Follows a recipe:** exact steps a person wrote (a calculator).
- **Learned from examples:** got good from lots of cases, so it copes with new ones. That's **AI** (face unlock).

**Try this:** find an app that gets better the more you use it — like video picks. It learned from examples.

Next: teach a robot yourself, and watch it slip up.
